## Historical audit: S0081

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/test/commons_163096530/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only chunk 2 of 3 is visible; the referenced photographs and renders are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 13, [0,222257) | The stated goal was an editable 3D reconstruction of one indoor photograph, including camera, framing, geometry and materials. The code’s scene interpretation was an old dormitory; that interpretation is not independent evidence of the photograph’s contents. |
| Student builds in line 13; `model_response`, line 15, [0,13810) | Code constructs multiple separate assets: three bunk assemblies, architecture, wardrobe, fireplace, radiator, clock and lamps. Bunk posts, rails, mattresses and ladders are grouped as parts; grouping does not verify physical contact. Procedural noise and bump nodes, colors and metallic settings specify materials, but their rendered appearance is unverified. No human pose is evidenced. |
| Student review and revision, line 13 | After step 1, the student described furniture as too small and leftward, the foreground bunk as obscuring the fireplace, and the floor as too pale. The next program changed lens 26→34, camera target, bunk placement, floor color and lighting. These discrepancies are student observations, not independently checked facts. |
| Student `model_response`, line 15, [0,13810); `execute`, line 16, [0,14512) | After step 2 the student reported back furniture still left/low, the foreground bunk absent, and floor/ceiling too light. The executed revision moved and retargeted the camera, repositioned and vertically scaled the foreground bunk, darkened surfaces and reduced lighting. Whether these changes corrected framing, occlusion or appearance is unknown. |
| Runner feedback in line 13; `execution_result`, line 17, [0,91853); `select`, line 18, [0,59) | Steps 1 and 2 were reported usable; step 3 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and Blender scene, and was selected. This establishes technical execution and selection, **not visual or geometric correctness**. The log reports 16 render samples despite code requesting 48. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 14, [0,3958) | The third student session completed with no tool calls, in a read-only sandbox with web and shell disabled. Render-driven revisions show autonomous exploration within the supplied interaction, not external investigation. |

**Teacher input and outcome.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or student receipt/adoption is visible in this chunk. The user/runner review instructions are visible, but are not evidence of a separate teacher. Technical build success is observed; formal scene-match success, partial correctness or algorithm failure cannot be determined. This was not an empty patch or a visible technical interruption.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, separating global camera adjustments from local object changes, grouping editable components, and checking primitive and material constraints make revisions traceable; execution alone cannot validate them. The bunk repositioning and darkening are task-specific hypotheses. Without the images or other chunks, actual object inventory, pose, connections, texture fidelity, camera slopes, lighting quality, and whether the final revision improved the match remain unresolved.
